# Postman compatibility

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-compat-doc.mjs from packages/core/test/pm-compat/cases.ts. Do not edit: change the rows and run `npm run gen:compat`. -->

What a pre-request or a post-response script can use of Postman's script
API in Wayfarer. Every row below is a test: its script runs in Node and in
the app's own worker in a browser, on every commit, and must show what the
row says. This file is written from those rows, and CI fails when it and
they differ. <!-- claim:C-040 -->

124 rows: 79 supported, 28 partial, 17 not supported.

- **Supported:** as in Postman.
- **Partial:** it is there, and the note says what differs.
- **Not supported:** calling it throws `WayfarerUnsupportedError` with the
  name of what was called and a link to its section here, unless the note
  says the name does not exist at all.

How scripts run, what they can reach and which may run is in
[`scripts.md`](scripts.md).

<a id="pm-environment"></a>

## `pm.environment`

| API | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `pm.environment.name` | Supported |  |
| `pm.environment.get` | Supported |  |
| `pm.environment.set` | Partial | Values are text: a number or an object that is set is read back as a string. In the app, a value set on a protected variable is encrypted into its vault secret; with the vault locked it is refused with a line in the console. |
| `pm.environment.unset` | Supported |  |
| `pm.environment.has` | Supported |  |
| `pm.environment.toObject` | Supported |  |
| `pm.environment.replaceIn` | Partial | Replaces from every scope, nearest first, as `pm.variables.replaceIn` does. |
| `pm.environment.clear` | Supported |  |

<a id="pm-variables"></a>

## `pm.variables`

| API | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `pm.variables.get` | Supported |  |
| `pm.variables.get (a folder's variable)` | Partial | Postman has no folder variables. Here a folder has them: `pm.variables` reads the nearest folder's value, which wins over the collection's and loses to the environment's. No scope of `pm` writes one. |
| `pm.variables.set` | Partial | Values are text: a number or an object that is set is read back as a string. |
| `pm.variables.has` | Supported |  |
| `pm.variables.toObject` | Supported |  |
| `pm.variables.replaceIn` | Supported |  |

<a id="pm-request"></a>

## `pm.request`

| API | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `pm.request.url.toString` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.url.getHost / getPath / getQueryString` | Partial | Read from the address as written, `{{variables}}` not replaced. The parts as lists (`protocol`, `host`, `path`, `query`) are not there. |
| `pm.request.url (assign)` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.method` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.headers.get` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.headers.has` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.headers.add` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.headers.upsert` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.headers.remove` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.headers.toObject / each` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.body (raw)` | Supported |  |
| `pm.request.body.update` | Partial | Text and `urlencoded` only. A multipart form and a file can be seen (`mode`) and not changed. |
| `pm.request (post-response)` | Partial | The request as it was sent: `{{variables}}` replaced, the Auth tab's header among the headers. A vault secret in it reads `***`. |

<a id="legacy"></a>

## Postman's older sandbox

| API | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `postman.setEnvironmentVariable` | Partial | Values are text: a number or an object that is set is read back as a string. |
| `postman.getEnvironmentVariable` | Supported |  |
| `postman.clearEnvironmentVariable` | Supported |  |
| `postman.clearEnvironmentVariables` | Supported |  |
| `postman.setGlobalVariable` | Partial | Values are text: a number or an object that is set is read back as a string. |
| `postman.getGlobalVariable` | Supported |  |
| `postman.clearGlobalVariable` | Supported |  |
| `postman.clearGlobalVariables` | Supported |  |
| `postman.setNextRequest` | Partial | Recorded. It has an effect in a collection run only, and there is none yet. |
| `postman.getResponseHeader` | Supported |  |
| `tests[name] = boolean` | Supported |  |
| `responseBody` | Supported |  |
| `responseCode` | Supported |  |
| `responseTime` | Supported |  |
| `responseHeaders` | Partial | Names are as the browser gives them: in lower case for a request sent from the page. |
| `request (legacy global)` | Partial | As `pm.request`: as composed in a pre-request script, as sent in a post-response script, a vault secret as `***`. `data` is the text of a raw body or the fields of a form. |
| `environment (legacy global)` | Supported |  |
| `globals (legacy global)` | Supported |  |
| `iteration` | Partial | Always 0: there is no collection run yet. |
| `response globals in a pre-request script` | Supported |  |
| `legacy library globals (_, CryptoJS, tv4, cheerio, xml2Json, Backbone)` | Not supported | ReferenceError: the names do not exist. Use `require` for the libraries that are there. |
